title: The Ironworks House to the Tikhvin Grave: Tchaikovsky, the Empire's Composer
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Votkinsk, the manager's house at the ironworks
stops.date_confidence: attested; 25 April 1840 by the Julian calendar then in use in Russia
stops.campa: In the manager's house of the Kamsko-Votkinsk ironworks, six hundred miles east of Moscow in the Urals, a mining engineer's wife bears her second son. Ilya Tchaikovsky runs the works for the crown. The household keeps an orchestrion that plays fragments of Mozart and Donizetti, and the boy hears the machine before he can name what it is doing to him. Udmurtia keeps the house as a museum. The birth is entered as 25 April: the Russian calendar runs twelve days behind the Western one and will run behind it until 1918.
suggested_refs: The Votkinsk ironworks manager's house, preserved as the Tchaikovsky Museum-Estate

stops.name: Votkinsk, the governess and the first piano
stops.date_confidence: Durbach engaged 1844 and the piano lessons with Maria Palchikova begin about 1845; neither is fixed to a month
stops.campa: The family engages a French governess, Fanny Durbach, who sets the boy to books and languages years ahead of his age and keeps his copybooks for the rest of her life. A local teacher, Maria Palchikova, gives him his first piano lessons at about five, and he outgrows her quickly. Both are the best the province has. Russia has no conservatory yet, and nobody at Votkinsk knows what to do with a child who cannot stop the music once the music has stopped. She is teaching a houseful of children and it is this one she is still describing forty years later.
stops.quote: Oh, this music, this music! Save me from it! It is here, here, and will not give me any peace.
stops.quote_source: Fanny Durbach's recollection of the child, reported in Modeste Tchaikovsky, Life & Letters of Peter Ilich Tchaikovsky, trans. Rosa Newmarch (1906), Part I, Ch. II; reported speech, not a document in his own hand
sources: Modeste Tchaikovsky, Life & Letters, trans. Newmarch (1906)
suggested_refs: Fanny Durbach's kept copybooks of her Votkinsk pupil

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the family arrives in the capital
stops.date_confidence: Tchaikovsky Research dates the departure from Votkinsk 26 Sept / 8 Oct 1848 and the arrival to November; Encyclopedia.com gives the move as 1850, a contradiction left open in the report
stops.campa: Ilya Tchaikovsky leaves the works and moves the household west, briefly to Moscow, then in November to the capital. Pyotr is enrolled as a day pupil and a private teacher takes over the piano. The hoped-for appointment does not come. Nobody in the capital marks the arrival. The same city that gave Francisco de Miranda a passport under Catherine in 1787, and that assembled Alexander von Humboldt's Asia expedition in 1829, has no use yet for an unemployed engineer from Vyatka.
suggested_refs: The Tchaikovsky family's first Saint Petersburg lodgings, November 1848

stops.name: Alapayevsk, the year back in the Urals
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1849; the day is not given in the reachable chronology
stops.campa: The appointment fails and Ilya takes a works post back east, so in May the family turns around and settles at Alapayevsk in the Urals. Pyotr is nine, already fixed on the piano, and now a thousand miles from any conservatory, in a country that does not have one. The posting does not last a year. The household moves at the speed of an engineer's employment rather than a boy's ear, and before he turns eleven the boy is sent back west to the capital alone.
suggested_refs: The Alapayevsk ironworks, Ilya Tchaikovsky's post of 1849

stops.name: Imperial School of Jurisprudence, the boarding years
stops.date_confidence: attested to September 1850; the day is not given
stops.campa: Ten years old, he is sent back alone to the capital and boarded at the Imperial School of Jurisprudence on the Fontanka, thirteen hundred kilometres from his family, to be made into a civil servant. He stays nine years. He sings in the school choir and is taught nothing else that a composer would need. The classmates he acquires in these corridors will follow him the length of his life, and eighty-six years after his death one version of his death will name them, without proof, as the men who ordered it.
suggested_refs: The Imperial School of Jurisprudence building on the Fontanka embankment

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, cholera takes his mother
stops.date_confidence: attested to 25 June 1854 by Tchaikovsky Research; Wikipedia gives June 1854 without a day
stops.campa: Cholera kills Aleksandra Tchaikovskaya in June. Her son is fourteen and inside the school walls when the word comes; he is not permitted to see her before the end. Two years later he writes to Fanny Durbach in France and reports it at that distance, flatly, in the register of a boy who has learned to hold a thing at arm's length before picking it up. The disease that takes her will be entered on his own death certificate thirty-nine years later, in this same city.
stops.quote: First I must give you some very sad news. A terrible grief befell us more than two years since. Four months after Zinaida's marriage my mother was taken ill with cholera.
stops.quote_source: Letter to Fanny Durbach, 1856, in Modeste Tchaikovsky, Life & Letters, trans. Newmarch
suggested_refs: The 1854 cholera epidemic in Saint Petersburg

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, titular counselor at the Ministry of Justice
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He graduates as a titular counselor and is posted to a clerk's desk in the Ministry of Justice, the exact outcome the School was built to produce. He keeps the desk four years. Music is, for the moment, the evening occupation of a young official who dances well and dresses beyond his salary. The Russian Musical Society opens theory classes in the city and he enrolls in them at twenty-one; the civil service holds him until 1863, when he walks out of it against every expectation his family has of him.
suggested_refs: The Ministry of Justice clerkship register, Saint Petersburg, 1859

stops.name: Paris, the end of the first circuit abroad
stops.date_confidence: the circuit is attested to 1861; no day dates survive in the reachable chronology and the August placement is inferred
stops.campa: At twenty-one he crosses Europe as secretary and interpreter to a businessman, his first journey out of Russia: Berlin, Hamburg, Antwerp, Brussels, London, Paris, in a matter of weeks. Paris closes the circuit. He will return to this city more often than to any other foreign capital, for opera, for a funeral, for exile from a marriage, for the conducting tours of his last decade. Marcel Proust is not yet born here; the Ballets Russes that Proust will watch in 1913 dances a repertoire descended from scores this clerk has not written yet.
suggested_refs: The 1861 European circuit as secretary and interpreter, Berlin to Paris

segments.name: The Conservatory and the Move to Moscow

stops.name: Saint Petersburg Conservatory, the Demidov house on the Moika
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1862; the September placement is the academic year, not a documented day
stops.campa: Anton Rubinstein opens the first conservatory in Russia and the Ministry clerk enrolls among its first students, in a wing of the Demidov house at the corner of Demidov Lane and the Moika embankment. The Theatre Square building the institution is known by today does not house it until 1896. He is a year late for Taras Shevchenko, buried out of this city in March 1861 with Dostoevsky and Turgenev walking behind the coffin. He resigns the civil service the next year and gives the work his whole week.
stops.quote: I only feel I must do the work for which I have a vocation. Whether I become a celebrated composer, or only a struggling teacher, 'tis all the same.
stops.quote_source: Letter to his sister, September 1862, in Modeste Tchaikovsky, Life & Letters, trans. Newmarch
sources: St Petersburg State Conservatory, official history (1862-66 location)
suggested_refs: The Demidov house on the Moika, first home of the Saint Petersburg Conservatory

stops.name: Kamenka, the sister's estate in the Ukrainian provinces
stops.date_confidence: the chronology dates the Kamenka habit only to 'from 1865'; the June placement is inferred from the pattern of summer visits
stops.campa: His sister Aleksandra has married into the Davydov family and keeps a large house at Kamenka, and from this year he goes there almost annually for decades. Among her children and the noise of an extended household he works better than he does in either capital. She is raising seven children in that house. She is the correspondent he writes to when the blackness comes down, and the letter he sends her from Moscow in November 1876 states it as plainly as he ever states it to anybody.
stops.quote: In my life, too, there are days, hours, weeks, aye, and months, in which everything looks black.
stops.quote_source: Letter to his sister Aleksandra Davydova, 8/20 November 1876 (Letter 513), in Life & Letters, trans. Newmarch; the widely circulated attribution to a nephew is an error
suggested_refs: The Davydov estate at Kamenka, his refuge from both capitals

stops.name: Pavlovsk, Strauss conducts the Characteristic Dances
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Johann Strauss the younger conducts the summer concerts at the Pavlovsk station outside the capital and puts the Characteristic Dances of an unknown conservatory student on his program. It is the first time Tchaikovsky hears his own orchestral writing played to a public. He is twenty-five and weeks from graduating with a silver medal. He has already told his brother Nikolai, who had assured him he was no genius, what he expects the family to make of him in the end.
stops.quote: Perhaps I shall not turn out a Glinka, but one thing I can assure you, you will be proud some day to own me as a brother.
stops.quote_source: Remark to his brother Nikolai, c. late 1862, reported in Modeste Tchaikovsky, Life & Letters, trans. Newmarch; reported speech, not a letter
suggested_refs: The Pavlovsk railway station concert hall, where Strauss conducted the summer seasons

stops.name: Moscow Conservatory, the harmony professor
stops.date_confidence: Nikolai Rubinstein's offer is autumn 1865 and the move January 1866; the Conservatory itself opens 1 September 1866 (O.S.), so the pool's '1865 professorship' is anachronistic
stops.campa: Nikolai Rubinstein makes the offer in the autumn of 1865, for the Moscow classes of the Musical Society; Tchaikovsky moves in January and the Conservatory formally opens that September. He teaches harmony for over a decade, lodging at first in Rubinstein's own rooms. Moscow gets his early symphonies and his first operas, written at night around the timetable. In 1868 he courts the Belgian soprano Desiree Artot and expects to marry her; she marries a Spanish baritone in Warsaw the following year.
suggested_refs: The Moscow Conservatory on Bolshaya Nikitskaya, opened September 1866

stops.name: Boston, the First Piano Concerto
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's 1874 is the year of composition and of Nikolai Rubinstein's denunciation
stops.campa: Nikolai Rubinstein, shown the First Piano Concerto in Moscow at Christmas 1874, calls it worthless and unplayable and demands it be rewritten. Tchaikovsky refuses to alter a note and sends it to Hans von Bulow instead. Von Bulow gives the first performance in Boston, under Benjamin Johnson Lang, on the far side of an ocean the composer has never crossed. The concerto is first heard in a country its author will not see for another sixteen years, played by a German pianist under an American conductor.
suggested_refs: The Boston Music Hall, 25 October 1875, Hans von Bulow soloist

stops.name: Bayreuth, the first Ring at the Festspielhaus
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 1876; the day of his attendance is not fixed in the reachable chronology
stops.campa: He travels to Franconia for the inaugural festival and the first complete Ring, sent partly as correspondent for a Moscow paper. Richard Wagner has built a theatre for one work and made Europe come to it. Tchaikovsky finds the theories more interesting than the results and says so in print. No meeting between the two men appears in any account reachable here. He leaves having seen what a composer can extract from a state, and goes home to a professor's salary.
suggested_refs: The 1876 inaugural Bayreuth Festival and the first complete Ring cycle

stops.name: Moscow, the best friend who must not be met
stops.date_confidence: the correspondence and allowance are attested to 1877; the January placement is inferred, the first letters falling around the turn of the year
stops.campa: Nadezhda von Meck, widow of a railway fortune, begins writing to him and settles an annual allowance on him with one condition attached: that the two never meet in person. The correspondence runs fourteen years. He dedicates the Fourth Symphony to her and, at her insistence, prints no name on it, only the words to my best friend. She will rent him rooms near her own in Florence and lend him her estates in her own absence, an intimacy conducted entirely through paper and empty houses.
suggested_refs: The Tchaikovsky and von Meck correspondence, 1877-1890

stops.name: Moscow, the marriage to Antonina Milyukova
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 1877; the pool does not give a day
stops.campa: Antonina Milyukova, a former student, writes him declarations and will not be refused; he marries her in July, in a state his brothers describe afterwards as a kind of sleepwalking. The marriage collapses within weeks. The couple live together about two and a half months in all, and then he goes to his sister and then abroad and they never live together again. Nine years earlier he had expected to marry Desiree Artot and been left. The Fourth Symphony and Eugene Onegin are both written across this wreckage.
suggested_refs: The Moscow marriage of July 1877 and the separation that followed within weeks

stops.name: Vienna, the flight from the marriage
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1877; no day given
stops.campa: He reaches Vienna in November with the violinist Iosif Kotek, who has followed him out of Russia. The flight becomes a year of wandering through Switzerland, Italy, and France, paid for out of von Meck's allowance. He is thirty-seven, a professor on leave, a husband in name only, and outside his own country for the foreseeable future. Vienna will hear his Violin Concerto four years from now, when it finally finds a soloist willing to play what Leopold Auer has called unplayable.
suggested_refs: Kotek's role in the 1877-78 flight from Russia

stops.name: Clarens, the Violin Concerto on the lake
stops.date_confidence: attested to March-April 1878; the pool's own entry misattributed the stay's output to The Maid of Orleans, begun here only in December 1878
stops.campa: On the shore of Lake Geneva, with Kotek at hand to test the writing, he composes the Violin Concerto in under a month. Leopold Auer, for whom he means it, declines it, and it waits three years for Adolph Brodsky to give it in Vienna under Hans Richter in December 1881. He comes back to this same shoreline in December to begin The Maid of Orleans. Kotek plays each passage back to him as it is written, which is why the solo part lies where a violinist's hand lies.
suggested_refs: Clarens on Lake Geneva, where the Violin Concerto was written in a month

stops.name: Florence, rooms rented near her own
stops.date_confidence: the never-meeting Florence arrangement belongs to November-December 1878; the pool's February 1878 date is a different, earlier stay
stops.campa: Von Meck takes a villa in Florence and rents him rooms near her own, close enough that the carriages pass. Neither of them stops. They do not meet once in November or December; the condition against meeting is hers. He works, she listens for the piano through the winter light, and the letters go on travelling between two houses a few streets apart. Earlier that year, at San Remo on the Ligurian coast, he had finished orchestrating the Fourth and completed Eugene Onegin.
suggested_refs: The villa von Meck rented in Florence, winter 1878, and the rooms taken for him nearby

stops.name: Maly Theatre, Moscow: Eugene Onegin
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Eugene Onegin has its first performance at the Maly, sung by students of the Moscow Conservatory under Nikolai Rubinstein, because Tchaikovsky wants no imperial theatre and no famous voices anywhere near it. He has set Pushkin, which a good part of Russian opinion holds to be sacrilege, and has written a letter scene for a girl who declares herself to a man who barely knows her and is refused. He married Antonina Milyukova in the middle of composing it. The tsar will order a new production in 1885.
suggested_refs: The student premiere of Eugene Onegin at the Maly Theatre, 29 March 1879

stops.name: Paris, the death of Nikolai Rubinstein
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Nikolai Rubinstein, who brought him to Moscow at twenty-five and told him at thirty-four that his concerto was unplayable rubbish, dies in Paris in March. Tchaikovsky comes to the funeral service of the man who made his working life possible and who conducted the first performances of Romeo and Juliet, Francesca da Rimini, and Eugene Onegin. The Piano Trio in A minor, inscribed to the memory of a great artist, comes directly out of this loss, written in a form he had said publicly that he disliked.
suggested_refs: The Piano Trio in A minor, 'to the memory of a great artist,' 1882

stops.name: Moscow, the 1812 Overture in a tent
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's 1880 is the year of composition
stops.campa: Commissioned for the consecration of the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, the overture is written in 1880 and first heard two years later, in a tent beside the still unfinished cathedral, under Ippolit Altani, during the All-Russia Arts and Industry Exhibition. It quotes the Marseillaise and it quotes the tsarist anthem. The Soviet Academy will publish it for fifty years with the tsarist anthem excised and the Marseillaise left standing. The Slavonic March is cut the same way.
suggested_refs: The exhibition tent beside the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, August 1882

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Order of St Vladimir
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1884; no month or day in the reachable sources, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: Alexander III grants him the Order of St Vladimir, fourth class, which carries hereditary nobility with it. The tsar who reads him as the national composer orders a new Eugene Onegin the next year and settles a lifetime pension of three thousand rubles on him. The engineer's son from the Votkinsk works now holds a rank in the imperial table. The money arrives as he gives up teaching and begins conducting, and it is what pays for the touring decade that follows.
suggested_refs: The Order of St Vladimir, fourth class, and the imperial pension of 1885

stops.name: Maydanovo, the first house of his own
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He rents a house on the Sestra river at Maydanovo, near Klin, his first fixed address after twenty years of rented rooms, hotel weeks, and other people's estates. It is close enough to Moscow for the concerts and far enough out that nobody calls. He is forty-four. He will move twice more inside a few miles of this spot, to Frolovskoye and then to Klin itself, and he will never live in a city again. Everything from Manfred onward is written from an address near this river.
suggested_refs: The rented house on the Sestra at Maydanovo, February 1885

stops.name: Moscow, the Manfred Symphony
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's 1885 is the year of composition, May to September
stops.campa: He writes the Manfred Symphony, on Byron's dramatic poem, between May and September 1885: a man wandering the Alps with a crime he will not name, refusing absolution at the end. Max Erdmannsdorfer conducts the first performance in Moscow the following March, six months after the score is finished. The gap between writing and first hearing is by now the ordinary rhythm of this career, and it is why the dates attached to his works in circulation are so often wrong by exactly one year.
suggested_refs: The Manfred Symphony, premiered under Max Erdmannsdorfer, Moscow, 23 March 1886

stops.name: Tiflis, the month with Anatoly
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1886; the diary entry quoted here is dated 1/13 April
stops.campa: His brother Anatoly is posted to the Caucasus as a civil servant and Pyotr spends April with him in Tiflis. He comes back in 1887 and again in 1889. The city is a month's remove from the imperial theatres and from everyone with an opinion about his music, and the diary he keeps here records the weather, the tea, and what he is reading rather than what he is writing. He is famous now in a way that makes an ordinary day worth setting down. The city gives him a public as well as a brother: the final version of Romeo and Juliet has its first performance here in 1886.
stops.quote: The weather was glorious in the morning, then deteriorated somewhat. Drank tea with Tolya.
stops.quote_source: Diaries, entry for Tuesday 1/13 April 1886, Tchaikovsky Research
suggested_refs: The Tiflis diaries of April 1886

stops.name: Bolshoi Theatre, Moscow: conducting Cherevichki
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1887; the pool does not give a day
stops.campa: He conducts Cherevichki at the Bolshoi in January, having first tried to hand the rehearsals and the whole run to a young musician the management proposed. The stagefright that kept him off the podium for years is not cured, only overridden. From this month he conducts his own music for the rest of his life. The Moscow theatre world he steps into is the one Suzanne Perrottet will find restless with Ballets Russes talk in 1912, and the one G. I. Gurdjieff advertises a ballet into in 1914.
stops.quote: I was immediately notified of this proposal, and P. M. P., who was then at the head of the theatre management in Moscow, asked me to confirm whether I was willing to entrust this young musician with the task of overseeing the rehearsals and conducting the orchestra during the first run of performances of Cherevichki.
stops.quote_source: Autobiographical Account of a Tour Abroad in the Year 1888, trans. Luis Sundkvist, Tchaikovsky Research
suggested_refs: Cherevichki at the Bolshoi, January 1887, his first sustained turn as conductor

stops.name: Baku, the Caspian crossing
stops.date_confidence: the Volga and Caspian route is attested to 1887; the month is inferred from the itinerary and the Astrakhan leg is tagged as reconstruction in the pool
stops.campa: He goes south to the Caucasus the long way, by river steamer from Nizhny Novgorod down the Volga toward Astrakhan and the delta, then across the Caspian by boat to Baku. It is the slowest route to Tiflis available and he takes it deliberately. The oil city is a waypoint and not a destination. For a week an older Russia unrolls past the deck rail: the empire he is by now the official musical voice of, seen at the speed of a paddle steamer from the water.
suggested_refs: The 1887 Volga and Caspian passage to the Caucasus

stops.name: Aachen, at Kondratyev's bedside
stops.date_confidence: attested, 15 to 27 July 1887
stops.campa: Nikolai Kondratyev, a friend of twenty years, is dying at Aachen, and Tchaikovsky comes and sits with him from the fifteenth of July to the twenty-seventh. He stays twelve days watching a man come apart by degrees in a German spa town. It is a journey undertaken for no reason except loyalty to somebody who can no longer do anything for him. Within six months of leaving this room he is on a podium in Leipzig, beginning the public half of his career.
suggested_refs: The Aachen spa, July 1887, and the death of Nikolai Kondratyev

stops.name: Leipzig Gewandhaus, the first European tour opens
stops.date_confidence: attested; he is 47 at this concert, not the 57 that circulates in the compiled sources
stops.campa: The first European conducting tour opens at the Gewandhaus on the fifth of January. He is forty-seven. In Leipzig he meets Brahms, rehearsing in the same hall, and Edvard Grieg, whom he takes to immediately and writes about at length afterwards, with the reservations of a man who has been taught form very strictly indeed. The tour runs on to Hamburg, Berlin, Prague, and Paris before spring. The composer who could not face an orchestra at thirty is now the chief exponent of his own music in Europe.
stops.quote: As for perfection of form, strictness and faultless logic in the elaboration of his themes (which, by the way, are always fresh, new, and stamped with the characteristic traits of Germano-Scandinavian nationality), let us not insist on looking for these in the famous Norwegian's music.
stops.quote_source: Autobiographical Account of a Tour Abroad in the Year 1888, on Edvard Grieg, trans. Luis Sundkvist, Tchaikovsky Research
sources: Berliner Philharmoniker, Tchaikovsky and the Berliner Philharmoniker
suggested_refs: The Gewandhaus concert of 5 January 1888, opening the first European tour

stops.name: London, St James's Hall in Piccadilly
stops.date_confidence: attested, 22 March 1888 (10 March O.S.), the Philharmonic Society's second concert; the pool's 20 March is two days out
stops.campa: At the Philharmonic Society's second concert of the season he conducts the Serenade for String Orchestra and the Theme and Variations from the Third Suite. English audiences are cordial and the English critical press stays cooler than the continental one. London first received him in 1861 as a clerk on a tourist circuit with a fortnight's itinerary and no reason to be noticed. He closes the tour here and sails home to a country that now reads his foreign reception as a national account being settled.
sources: Tchaikovsky Research, London / Serenade for String Orchestra
suggested_refs: St James's Hall, Piccadilly, Philharmonic Society concert of 22 March 1888

stops.name: Frolovskoye, the leased house and the felled trees
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1888; no day given
stops.campa: He leases a house at Frolovskoye, a village nearer the forest than Maydanovo, and inside eighteen months writes the Fifth Symphony and The Sleeping Beauty in it. He plants trees on the property with his own hands. The owner has the surrounding wood cut down while he is living there, and he takes it as a bereavement and says so to everyone. He is fond enough of this house to lose his temper over its landscape, which is more than he has ever said about a city.
suggested_refs: The leased house at Frolovskoye near Klin, where the Fifth Symphony was written

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Fifth Symphony conducted
stops.date_confidence: the pool gives the year only; the standard date is 5/17 November 1888 and the day is not asserted here
stops.campa: He conducts the first performance of the Fifth Symphony in the capital in November, the same year as the European tour. It is the first of his symphonies he brings to an audience from the podium himself, after fifteen years of letting other men present his work. The city that holds this concert also holds the School of Jurisprudence that made him a clerk, the Conservatory that made him a musician, and the cemetery that will take him in five years.
suggested_refs: The premiere of the Fifth Symphony, Saint Petersburg, November 1888

stops.name: Mariinsky Theatre, The Sleeping Beauty
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1890; the pool fixes no day
stops.campa: The Sleeping Beauty opens at the Mariinsky in January, choreographed by Marius Petipa, commissioned directly by the director of the imperial theatres. Court ballet is state business and he is now the composer the state uses for it. Fifteen years on, Isadora Duncan will dance barefoot in this city within days of Bloody Sunday, with Diaghilev, Fokine, Pavlova, and Kschessinska in the seats, and the company Diaghilev builds out of that room will carry these same scores west into another century.
suggested_refs: The Petipa production of The Sleeping Beauty, Mariinsky Theatre, January 1890

stops.name: New York, the opening of the Music Hall
stops.date_confidence: attested to opening night, 5 May 1891; the American visit runs 26 April to 21 May
stops.campa: He crosses the Atlantic to conduct at the opening festival of Andrew Carnegie's new Music Hall on Fifty-seventh Street, leading his own Marche solennelle on opening night with the New York Music Society orchestra. American audiences and the American press treat him as a celebrity, which Europe never quite managed, and he writes home astonished at the size of the reception and the size of the buildings. The hall will carry his opening night in its founding story for a hundred years and more.
sources: Carnegie Hall, 'Five Facts About Carnegie Hall's Opening Night'
suggested_refs: Opening night of Carnegie's Music Hall, 5 May 1891

stops.name: Philadelphia, Academy of Music: the last American concert
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The American tour ends at the Academy of Music in Philadelphia, the last concert he conducts on the continent. Three days later he sails for home on the Prince Bismarck. Inside one month he has conducted in New York, in Baltimore on the fifteenth and sixteenth, and here, and been received at the Russian Embassy in Washington. He does not come back. The concerto whose first performance he could not attend in Boston sixteen years earlier now belongs to a country that can put a face to it.
sources: Broad Street Review, When Tchaikovsky came to Philadelphia
Classical Music Guide Forums (Baltimore and Washington, weak single source)
suggested_refs: The Academy of Music, Philadelphia, 18 May 1891, and the sailing of the Prince Bismarck

stops.name: Klin, the last house
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1892; three different coordinates for this house circulate within about 1.4 km and the report prints all three
stops.campa: He takes a house on the edge of Klin, on the Moscow highway, his last address. The Sixth Symphony is written at the desk in the upstairs room. Within a year of his death his brother Modest turns the house into a memorial museum and opens it in December 1894 with the archive, the library, and the rooms left standing as they stood, the oldest memorial music museum in Russia. In 1941 German troops will billet on the ground floor while the collection sits evacuated in Votkinsk, where he was born.
suggested_refs: The Tchaikovsky State House-Museum at Klin, opened 9 December 1894

stops.name: Mariinsky Theatre, Iolanta and The Nutcracker
stops.date_confidence: attested to December 1892; the day given here follows the standard chronology and the pool fixes only the month
stops.campa: Iolanta and The Nutcracker are given together at the Mariinsky in December, a one-act opera and a two-act ballet on the same enormous evening. The reception is lukewarm and the ballet is judged a slight thing beside The Sleeping Beauty. In the century that follows it becomes the most performed theatrical work of the Western Christmas and pays the annual bills of ballet companies on three continents. He is dead eleven months after the premiere and learns none of it.
suggested_refs: The double bill of Iolanta and The Nutcracker, Mariinsky Theatre, December 1892

stops.name: Cambridge, the Senate House doctorate
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1893; the pool fixes no day
stops.campa: Cambridge gives him an honorary doctorate of music in the Senate House, alongside Saint-Saens, Bruch, and Boito, with Grieg awarded in absentia. He crosses to England for the ceremony, one of the last journeys he makes abroad. Paris elected him a corresponding member of the Academie des Beaux-Arts the year before. He is fifty-three, in academic scarlet, in a university town, four months from death, and the honours of the West have all arrived inside eighteen months.

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Sixth Symphony conducted
stops.date_confidence: attested; 16 October 1893 by the Julian calendar
stops.campa: He conducts the first performance of the Sixth Symphony in the capital on the twenty-eighth of October, a work that ends with a slow movement dying out where a finale is supposed to stand. The reception is respectful and puzzled. Nine days later he is dead, and the memorial concert plays the identical notes to a city that now hears them as a farewell written in advance. Every account of his death since, official and dissident alike, argues backwards from this symphony.
suggested_refs: The premiere of the Sixth Symphony, 28 October 1893, conducted by the composer

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the glass of water at Leiner's
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1 November 1893 in the account that became official
stops.campa: At Leiner's restaurant on Nevsky Prospekt he drinks a glass of unboiled water in front of companions who tell him not to, in a city that has cholera in it. The official account turns on this glass: four days of illness follow, and then death. Every argument against the official account turns on it too, because a man who lost his mother to cholera at fourteen knew exactly what unboiled water meant in Saint Petersburg in 1893. The gesture is carelessness or it is something else, and the sources do not settle which.
suggested_refs: Leiner's restaurant on Nevsky Prospekt, 1 November 1893

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, Malaya Morskaya: the death
stops.date_confidence: attested; 25 October 1893 by the Julian calendar, a dual dating and not a contradiction
stops.campa: He dies at three in the morning in the apartment on Malaya Morskaya, fifty-three years old, nine days after the premiere. Cholera is entered as the cause. Eighty-six years later the musicologist Aleksandra Orlova publishes a secondhand account of a court of honour: old classmates from the School of Jurisprudence condemning him to poison himself in order to bury a scandal about his homosexuality. Medical historians dispute the cholera and the arsenic both. The contemporaneous records are contradictory and incomplete, and the question stays open.
sources: Washington Post, 'Was Tchaikovsky Forced to Commit Suicide?' (1981)
suggested_refs: The Malaya Morskaya apartment where he died, 6 November 1893

stops.name: Kazan Cathedral, sixty thousand for six thousand places
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Alexander III pays the funeral costs himself and grants Kazan Cathedral, normally kept for state occasions, for the service. The cathedral holds six thousand. Some sixty thousand apply for tickets and about eight thousand are pressed inside. No private subject of the empire has been buried on these terms. The tsar who gave him a rank and a pension is burying a composer the way the state buries a general, and the crowd along Nevsky Prospekt has come for the music rather than the rank.
suggested_refs: The funeral at Kazan Cathedral, 9 November 1893

stops.name: Tikhvin Cemetery, among the composers
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool carries two coordinates for the plot, 30.3897 and 30.3886, about sixty metres apart
stops.campa: He is buried at Tikhvin Cemetery inside the Alexander Nevsky Monastery, in ground that holds Glinka, Mussorgsky, Borodin, and Dargomyzhsky, with Rimsky-Korsakov to follow. The plot closes a line that starts with an orchestrion in a Votkinsk nursery and a small boy asking to be saved from the music in his head. In 1932 the Soviet state makes the cemetery a sculpture museum, and the graves of the men he measured himself against for fifty years become an exhibit with an entrance fee.
suggested_refs: The Necropolis of Masters of Art at Tikhvin Cemetery, Alexander Nevsky Lavra
